outcome: The conjecture as stated (a fixed non-square, non-(-1) integer is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes) remains open and unproved unconditionally; the only claimed full proof found is conditional on a new, itself-unproven hypothesis, and other 2024-2026 work addresses related but distinct questions (refinements of the conjecture's finer structure, and an 'on average over a' version), not the stated conjecture for a fixed a.
summary: I found no result in the window (26 Jan 2024 - 22 Sep 2026) that changes the status of Artin's conjecture on primitive roots as literally stated: that a fixed integer which is neither a perfect square nor -1 is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes. The most significant candidate, flagged by triage, is Murty and Naik's arXiv preprint 'A non-abelian large sieve and Artin's primitive root conjecture' (arXiv:2608.21573, submitted 25 Aug 2026), which states it proves the full conjecture 'assuming the non-abelian large sieve inequality' -- a new hypothesis the authors themselves have not proved (they only give partial/unconditional progress toward it via duality techniques). This is structurally the same kind of result as Hooley's 1967 GRH-conditional proof: a conditional proof resting on an unproved hypothesis, not a change in the conjecture's actual open/closed status, and I found no evidence of expert digestion or acceptance establishing the sieve inequality itself. I classified this as not changing the status (still `open`), by analogy with how Hooley's classical conditional proof does not make Wikipedia call the conjecture resolved. The second item triage found, Goldmakher-Martin-Peringuey's 'Refinements of Artin's primitive root conjecture' (arXiv:2502.19601, Feb 2025), explicitly poses new, finer conjectures about the distribution of the multiplicative order that 'contain Artin's original conjecture as a special case' -- i.e. it changes the question (a related/refined problem), and proves its own refinements under GRH plus some unconditional partial results; it does not touch the literal conjecture as stated beyond what was already known via Hooley. I also found Klurman-Shparlinski-Teravainen, 'On Artin's conjecture on average and short character sums' (arXiv:2412.13355, submitted 17 Dec 2024, published in Bulletin LMS May 2025), which proves the asymptotic predicted by Artin's conjecture holds for almost all a in a growing range -- an average-case/variant statement over a, not a resolution for any single fixed a, and it explicitly improves on Stephens (1969), a pre-existing average-case literature distinct from the stated conjecture. None of these three papers, nor the current Wikipedia article on the conjecture, nor any other source I found, mentions any AI system, machine-learning tool, or automated theorem prover contributing to the mathematics; all read as traditional analytic/algebraic number theory. A search on AI benchmarks turned up only that Artin's conjecture appears as a test problem in the FrontierMath benchmark used to evaluate AI mathematical reasoning, with no claim that any model produced progress on it. Given the scope rule in section 3.1, I treat both the refinement paper and the 'on average' paper as related-but-distinct problems rather than cases of the stated conjecture, and the Murty-Naik preprint as a conditional result in the same unresolved pattern as Hooley's, so the conjecture's status has not moved: `open`, `no_change_found` true.
competing_reading: One could argue the Murty-Naik preprint should be `claimed` with `resolution_direction` `confirmed`, on the reasoning that a genuinely new conditional proof of the *full* conjecture (rather than a further partial/average result) is itself a notable event even if the condition is unproved -- this would parallel treating Hooley's 1967 result as a landmark despite being GRH-conditional. Against this: Hooley's hypothesis (GRH) is a widely-studied standard conjecture with its own extensive support, while the 'non-abelian large sieve inequality' is newly introduced in this very paper with only partial unconditional support shown by the same authors, making the conditional proof considerably weaker evidentially and not yet vetted by any expert digestion. I judged this closer to a conditional-on-a-new-unestablished-hypothesis result (not yet a `claimed` proof of the actual conjecture, since the load-bearing hypothesis is itself open and unreviewed) than to a landmark conditional proof, but a future reviewer who finds independent scrutiny of the non-abelian large sieve inequality, or expert commentary treating this preprint as a serious conditional resolution, might reasonably upgrade this to `progress` or `claimed`.
what_would_settle_it: Expert commentary (a survey update, a blog post by a number theorist, or peer review) assessing whether Murty and Naik's 'non-abelian large sieve inequality' is a plausible/well-supported hypothesis comparable in status to GRH, which would clarify whether their conditional proof is comparable to Hooley's landmark result or a much weaker conditional claim; also, any later paper either proving or disproving the non-abelian large sieve inequality itself.
